I've been working this same land for 20 years. My 2.6 mu feeds my wheat in winter and maize in summer — the same plot, rotated. Some of my family earns money in town now, so I manage most of this myself. I know my fields. My well is reliable. I don't gamble.

**Wheat:** I'll sow in mid-October after maize is off the field. I've been using an improved variety for years — consistent germination, good resistance to the cold snaps we get here. I'll do rotary tillage to work in the maize stubble. Three irrigations: before winter sets in, at jointing, and at heading. I've learned not to skimp on the winter water — it matters more than people say. I'll split my nitrogen between base application and a topdressing at jointing. Two rounds of pesticide — one for powdery mildew in spring, one for aphids before harvest.

**Maize:** Right after I sell the wheat in June, I plant. No-tillage — I can't afford to lose days, and my soil doesn't need it mid-season. Hybrid seed, same one the seed shop in town recommends and that my neighbors have been using. Three irrigations: when seedlings are young, at tasseling, and during grain fill. I'll do a heavy nitrogen top-dress at the big bell stage. The yield difference is real when you do that right.
